This weak, mostly-boundary-driven neuron fires on segment-break tokens in scraped web/boilerplate text — chiefly sentence-final ".\n" newlines, plus commas and connectives (" and", ",") that join items in list-like enumerations (the same ".\n"/"?\n"/'"\n' form also drives strong negative activation, so it is a punctuation/newline boundary detector rather than a semantic one).

L12·N3493unmasked layer
This neuron has no clear semantic theme — it fires weakly and diffusely on the middle token of common fixed multi-word collocations ("a **variety** of", "be **able** to", "enables **you** to", "**aren**'t") and on hyphen/underscore-joined fragments inside compound identifiers, and is suppressed by sentence-initial discourse words and terminal punctuation.

Fires at the punctuation that opens attributed/quoted speech — most strongly on the colon after a speaker name in transcript-style dialogue (e.g. "Wang Fei:", "~shane:"), and more weakly on opening curly quote marks and paragraph-final periods before a new quoted line (the same opening-quote token can also strongly suppress it, so the sign is context-dependent).

L14·N4266unmasked layer
This is a low-magnitude, syntax-position neuron: it peaks on mid-sentence grammatical glue that opens a new predicate/modifier — relativizer "that", modals "might"/"can", determiner "a", adjective "automatic", or the clause-closing comma — while being strongly suppressed on prepositions/conjunctions that close fixed multiword expressions ("receipt of", "as soon as", "and begin", "rear of the formation when").

L14·N5981unmasked layer
This neuron fires on short function words (contracted auxiliaries, modals, determiners, prepositions like "'d", "for", "might", "this", "a", "need") occurring in the first few tokens of a document/message opening, with activation decaying over the following words — i.e. it marks the opening-clause position rather than any semantic content.

L31·N3175unmasked layer
Fires on tokens that continue an in-progress phrase mid-sentence (e.g. the head noun after a modifier, "that" after a noun, "then"/"all" linking clauses) in informal user-written prose, and is strongly suppressed at sentence/paragraph-initial capitalized words like "In"/"How" that begin a new sentence — i.e. it tracks mid-clause continuation vs. fresh-sentence onset rather than any specific topic.
